configurations._comment: Serves the built bundle from dist/. Use this rather than wilson-dev when measuring network behaviour: `vite` dev serves every module unbundled, which fills the browser's 250-entry resource-timing buffer before the app has finished booting and makes any later request invisible. Run `npm run build` first.
configurations.name: wilson-preview-build

configurations._comment: BC1 (Bins on the cloud, schema + plumbing): this worktree's dev server on the bundle's port, signed in as the dev fixtures' tester (VITE_DEV_AUTOLOGIN=tester, VITE_DEV_FIXTURES=1 in its .env.local). The Bins tab shows the fixtures' bins — the one visible change of BC1.
configurations.name: bc1-worktree

configurations._comment: BC2 (Bins on the cloud, the desktop app signed in): this worktree's dev server on the bundle's port, signed in as the dev fixtures' tester (VITE_DEV_AUTOLOGIN=tester, VITE_DEV_FIXTURES=1 in its .env.local). The fixtures show the footage locations and the company's switch in Settings, Storage; the desktop's own file reads need the Electron app signed in to wilson-dev.
configurations.name: bc2-worktree

configurations._comment: BC3 (Bins on the cloud, the browser): this worktree's dev server on the bundle's port, signed in as the dev fixtures' tester (VITE_DEV_AUTOLOGIN=tester, VITE_DEV_FIXTURES=1 in its .env.local). The Bins tab shows the catalogue a browser gets; `?bins=browser` on the URL makes the fixtures answer as the cloud does in a browser (no row reachable). Proven by fetching src/tools/rabbit_v0.1.0/bins/browserCatalogue.js, a BC3-only module, from it.
configurations.name: bc3-worktree

configurations._comment: V1: the SIGN-IN screens, without editing .env.local. Vite ranks a variable already in the process environment above .env files, so this sets VITE_DEV_AUTOLOGIN to a value the app ignores (App.jsx signs in only on the exact string tester) and the auth screens render while .env.local still says tester. Port 5246; the signed-in server stays on 5245.
configurations.name: v1-auth
